events.title: Alfred the Great dies
events.description: Alfred, king of the Anglo-Saxons, died after a reign spent defending Wessex against the Vikings. His fortified burhs, navy and promotion of learning in English laid foundations for a unified England.
events.html: Alfred, king of the Anglo-Saxons, died after a reign spent defending Wessex against the Vikings. His fortified burhs, navy and promotion of learning in English laid foundations for a unified England.

events.title: The Uprising of Asen and Peter against Byzantine rule begins
events.description: On the feast day of Saint Demetrius of Thessaloniki, the brothers Theodore-Peter and Ivan Asen led the Bulgarians and Vlachs of the Balkan Mountains in a revolt against Byzantine rule, sparked by taxation. By 1187 they had established the Second Bulgarian Empire.

events.title: The army proclaims John VI Kantakouzenos emperor, starting a civil war
events.description: The army and supporters of John VI Kantakouzenos, largely drawn from the land-holding aristocracy, proclaimed him emperor, effectively starting a civil war against the regency for the boy John V Palaiologos. The regency responded by crowning John V in November.

events.title: Tvrtko I is crowned the first king of Bosnia
events.description: Tvrtko I, ban of Bosnia since 1353, had himself crowned king of Bosnia and Serbia at Mile, claiming to be heir to Serbia's extinct Nemanjić dynasty. The exact day of the coronation is uncertain.

events.title: Yi Sun-sin holds the Myeongnyang Strait with 13 ships
events.description: With only 13 ships left after the defeat at Chilcheollyang, Admiral Yi Sun-sin of the Joseon Navy routed a Japanese fleet of 300 ships near Jindo Island. The Japanese had been sailing to support their army's advance toward the Joseon capital, Hanyang.

events.title: The First Continental Congress adjourns in Philadelphia
events.description: Delegates of twelve of the Thirteen Colonies had met at Carpenters' Hall since 5 September. They had gathered after the British blockaded Boston Harbor and Parliament passed the Intolerable Acts in answer to the Boston Tea Party.

events.title: The Erie Canal opens
events.description: Governor DeWitt Clinton set off from Buffalo on the newly completed Erie Canal, which linked Lake Erie to the Hudson River over 363 miles. Cheap transport to the Midwest made New York City the nation's leading port.
events.html: Governor DeWitt Clinton set off from Buffalo on the newly completed Erie Canal, which linked Lake Erie to the Hudson River over 363 miles. Cheap transport to the Midwest made New York City the nation's leading port.

events.title: The gunfight near the O.K. Corral erupts in Tombstone
events.description: Wyatt, Virgil and Morgan Earp and Doc Holliday shot dead Billy Clanton and Tom and Frank McLaury in about 30 seconds in Tombstone, Arizona. The fight became the Wild West's most famous legend.

events.title: Ngô Đình Diệm proclaims the Republic of Vietnam
events.description: After a heavily rigged referendum deposed the former emperor Bảo Đại, Ngô Đình Diệm proclaimed the Republic of Vietnam in the south. US support for the regime drew America into the Vietnam War.

events.title: Russian forces end the Moscow theatre siege with gas
events.description: Special forces pumped an incapacitating chemical into a Moscow theatre where Chechen militants held some 850 hostages. The attackers were killed, but about 130 hostages died, mostly from the gas's effects.
